utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Case Number IT-01-47-T, the Prosecutor versus Enver Hadzihasanovic and Amir Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Could we have the appearances for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution today, Mr. Stefan Waespi, Daryl Mundis, and our case manager, Janet Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Could we have the appearances for Defence counsel. I can see that one member of the Defence is missing.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. On behalf of Enver Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, counsel; Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel; and Alex Demirdjian, our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the appearances for the other Defence team, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Nermin Mulalic, legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will be resuming with our hearing. I would like to great everyone present, members of the Prosecution, Defence counsel, the accused, and everyone in or around the courtroom. We'll be starting this hearing at a few minutes past 3.00. I will now ask the usher to call the witness into the courtroom; he has just arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, sir, you may sit down. I will now give the floor to Defence counsel. They will continue with their examination-in-chief. As far as I have understood, they require about ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Jusufspahic.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: You will recall that yesterday we left off when you said that in late July or early August you visited two brigades, the 312th and the 306th. Would you please look the set of documents under IV where it says "Mujahedins," and would you look at documents 1 and 2 and tell me whether you recognise them.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are documents from the operations organ of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Who drew up these documents?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The proposal was drawn up by the operations officers, together with the chief of staff. This was done in the staff.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, is the document you are looking at numbered 1360? It's under section IV, the title is "Mujahedin"?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Excuse me, I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: The document is 1360, that's under number 1; and under number 2 is document DH270. These are documents which are found in the last section of the bundle numbered IV and entitled "Mujahedin."

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Mujahedin, 1360, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's the first document, 1360. And under number 2 is document DH270. Now I'm asking you, do you recognise these documents and what are these documents?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just have a look, please. This is a report that I drew up myself after visiting these two brigades.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Jusufspahic, did there come a time when you were transferred from the operations organ of the 3rd Corps to another duty, and if so tell us when and where you were transferred.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was transferred from the operations and training organ to the joint commission.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And after that?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the joint commission ceased its work, a joint command was established with HVO officers.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when, as you explained, the joint command ceased working, did you return to the operations and training organ?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: During August 1993, were you transferred to a new duty?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us to what duty you were appointed then.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order was written in mid-August, but I took over my duties in late August and this was in the 306th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you became commander of the 306th Mountain Brigade, did any changes take place in that brigade, and, if so, can you tell us what happened actually.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, changes did take place in that brigade. There were fighters from the so-called Krajina, Siprage, Kotor Varos, and other places. They were all more or less in one battalion. And together with fighters from other units and this battalion, the 27th Mountain Brigade was formed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In that period of time, do you know whether fighters continued to be transferred from your unit to other units in the way you described in your report which you delivered to the corps command after your visit in early August? Were there any other such visits?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was quite clear to me when I arrived in that territory what the problem was, and the problem continued. The problem of soldiers moving to other units continued. This is a transit area, it's on the road between Zenica and Travnik, and many units passed through.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufspahic, would you please look at documents 5 and 6 and tell me whether the superior commands became involved and suggested that certain transfers be made and approved the transfer of men from one unit to another.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 5 and 6?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's in the same section. It's 1404 and 1389, those are the numbers of the documents.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Will you please repeat your question once again.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: My question was: Do you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as document number 5 is concerned, we don't have the English translation. So it would be perhaps be useful if you asked for the relevant paragraph to be read out. I only have the B/C/S version of this document. I don't have the English version. So perhaps you could point out the relevant sections to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Mr. President, for not drawing your attention to this. I was just about to ask the witness to read the text in document 1404 up to the words "Commander Enver Hadzihasanovic" so that Your Honours would be able to know what this is about. And later on, we will submit a translation of the entire document.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, would you please read the heading and the brief letter by the commander.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina" --

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please read the upper part of the text where it says "commander of the 3rd Corps."

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me see.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness be asked to read slowly.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you tell me whether you found the document which is numbered 1404 and is in section 5 of 4. So would you please read the top part of the document above the signature of Commander Enver Hadzihasanovic. Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Please find attached the order of the staff of the VKOS [as interpreted] of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Strictly confidential number 14/75-91 of the 17th of August, 1993, in connection with the voluntary transfer of fighters from the territory of the municipality of Bosanska Krajina in the 27th Motorised Brigade." I will read it again. "Please find attached an order of the staff of the supreme command of the armed forces of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Strictly confidential, number 14/75-91, dated the 17th of August, 1993, in connection with the voluntary transfer of soldiers from the territory of the municipality of Bosanska Krajina to the 27th Motorised Brigade. Execute the order immediately and act in compliance with its provisions. Commander Enver Hadzihasanovic."

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1993 were you aware of this order coming from the staff of the supreme command and the order by Commander Hadzihasanovic, and was that in fact the year in which significant transformations of the unit of the 3rd Corps took place?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course I am familiar with this order because I received it myself; I was already in this brigade. And I know about these changes. This was a continuing process of raising the brigades up to manpower level and so on.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And these changes and transfers of soldiers from one unit to another, did they give rise to certain problems for the brigade commanders?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they often did because the tasks were always the same. Sometimes, because of a lack of familiarity with the situation on the ground, a unit would be weakened and the soldiers would go to other units.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufspahic, when you were appointed commander of the 306th Brigade, did you know at that time that the El Mujahedin detachment had been formed by an order of the supreme command?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived in that brigade, I didn't know about that order, really.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And when as the brigade commander did you learn that such a detachment existed?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday I was already there in that area and I'd seen those people up there, but I didn't make the connection. I didn't realise that that was the unit in question. The first time I learned that this was a detachment was when I received the order on the resubordination of that unit to me for the purpose of carrying out combat activities. And it then became clear to me that that unit was to carry out certain tasks together with me.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please now take a look at the document and tell me first what happened. Was that unit resubordinated to you in fact?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. I waited for its superior officer to come to my command, but nobody arrived.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Until when were you the commander of the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until the first week of November in that same year; that's when I was wounded.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Was the El Mujahedin detachment ever resubordinated to the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was commander of that unit, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufspahic, please tell me, while you were the commander of the 306th Brigade, did you ever receive a request from the command of the 3rd Corps, or rather the operations group of Bosanska Krajina, to answer questions connected to some events dating from June 1993?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I received a written order asking me to provide certain information.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufspahic, please tell me, what did you know happened in June 1993?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said previously, in that period after being in the joint command in Travnik I was deployed in the operations centre. I wasn't there all the time, but that's where my post was, where it had been before I'd left it. And what I knew about these combat activities are only that there was strong HVO forces in the area where the fighting took place and that heavy fighting took place there lasting for more than a day.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you received this request to verify certain information, who did you assign this task to?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the system of the chain of command, you assign such tasks to the assistant for security; that's what I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did your security organ inform you and provide you with answers to the questions put to you by the supreme -- by the superior command?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether you're aware of this, but the security organ usually has a parallel system of reporting. In addition to the system of reporting it goes through the commanders. They would inform the commanders when they thought this was necessary. I received a written report on the situation.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Did you have reason to doubt the truth of the information provided to you by your security organ?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I had no reason to doubt the truth of the information, in particular because I had no other information about the matter. And those events took place before I arrived on the scene and I had spoke to other officers in the command, too. And the information I had is the information I put down on paper.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: What did you do with that report?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I drafted a report for the corps command.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at document that follows, number 7; the number of the document is 1498.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is that the report that your security organ provided to you as a response to the request made by the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have the same situation. Could the witness read the document out since we don't have a translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Go ahead, Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In order to avoid any confusion, this document has already been admitted into evidence. The document number is DK17, and we do have the English translation; it was admitted into evidence for Mr. Kubura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will try to locate DK17. We could perhaps place it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Jusufspahic, your security organ provided you with this document and you forwarded it to the 3rd Corps. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's correct. I'm familiar with this document. I'm familiar with the contents of the document; that's what I mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: As you have just said, you had no other information. Did you feel the need to conduct additional investigations or to try and obtain other information after you had been provided with this report by your security organ?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it wasn't necessary. I was new there. There were people who were performing their duties. There was ongoing combat activity at the time, so I really didn't feel the need to launch any further investigations.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you please also have a look at document under number 8 and 9, and could you tell me whether these are new appointments that concerned you and your chief of staff.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. This document concerns my transfer to other duties as well as the transfer of my chief of staff to other duties. And as you can see new people were appointed to posts.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to thank you for your assistance. I apologise for having taken up a little more than the 15 minutes I thought I would need to conclude my examination-in-chief, but this concludes my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Would Mr. Kubura's Defence like to take the floor to put any Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond questions to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We only have a few questions to clarify certain issues that were raised by documents shown to the witness, and there were also certain issues raised by the translation of that document into English. Could the witness have a look at the document he had before him a minute ago. It's a document that can be found in section 4, document 1. The number of the document is 1360.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you have the document?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: If we have a look at the document we can see that you drafted it and signed it. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I drafted and signed the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Please have a look at 2 of this document. "Proposed measures" is the heading.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Under item 1 it says that in the area of Bijelo -- it says that given a relatively small number of unit of Arabs left behind by the 7th Muslim Brigade which has left this area is operating among the ones in Bijelo Bucje sector?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: You also said they were operating in the zone of responsibility of the 312th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at the line 2. There are brackets there. It says "remained behind the 7th Muslim Brigade which has left the territory."

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: If I have understood this correctly, this unit of 30 Arab soldiers was there after the 7th Muslim Brigade had left Bijelo Bucje?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I can tell you about this because I was present. I can tell you what happened. After having visited the defence lines of the Karaula Battalion, after arranging the defence lines in the forest, usually one has a meeting in the command of that battalion. Problems are discussed, requests are discussed, and after having visited the lines I was supposed to continue to the 306th. The commander of the battalion mentioned the problem of the 30 soldiers who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the 312th?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he mentioned the problems of the soldiers who were there in his zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we have a look at the English translation on page 2 under the heading "proposed measures," in the English translation it says: "Left behind by the 7th Muslim Brigade." It appears that the 7th Muslim Brigade left them behind; that's what the translation seems to say. But the Bosnian version doesn't say that, so I think we have a problem that we have already encountered. We would like to resolve the problem by following the procedure we usually follow to make sure that there is no confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Are you telling us that in the English translation that I have before you [as interpreted] it seems that the 30 soldiers were left behind by the 7th Muslim Brigade and that item 5, that they were with the 7th Muslim Brigade; whereas the B/C/S text, and this has been confirmed by the witness, they weren't left behind, they were behind in a geographical sense. Is that how you're interpreting this text?

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're absolutely correct, Your Honour, and thank you. We have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We might go back to this subject when other questions are put. Yes, Mr. Registrar. Could you ask CLSS to revise the translation and to provide us with a translation of paragraph 1 under the heading "proposed measures" which is page 2 of document number 1360. We require an explanation or a re-translation of "left behind." Does this correspond to the B/C/S text or is this a free interpretation. I will now give the floor to Mr. Mundis so that he can proceed with his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: My name is Daryl Mundis and along with my colleagues here today I represent the Prosecution in this case. And I do note, sir, for the record you may recall I met with you in Sarajevo in November 2003 and spoke to you for about two hours on that occasion. And at that time, you did not provide us with a signed statement, having informed us that you would be called as a witness by the Defence in this case. I just wanted to put that on the record and also re-introduce myself to you. My purpose here today, sir, in asking you some questions is not in any way to confuse you, so I simply ask in the event you don't understand any of the questions that I am asking, please tell me that and I will rephrase the questions so that you do understand. I think it's in everyone's best interests that we all are able to communicate as clearly as possible. I'm going to ask you a few questions beginning with a subject that you spoke about late yesterday as well as earlier this afternoon, namely the issue of the Mujahedin. And I would ask you, sir, if it's all right with you, that when I use the term "Mujahedin," I'm referring to armed foreign fighters who were present in Central Bosnia during late 1992 and 1993. So there may be some confusion about this, but I want to be clear with you at the outset that when I use the term "Mujahedin," I'm referring to armed foreign fighters. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me go then, sir, back to what you began talking about yesterday, these two occasions you told us about where you first encountered these Mujahedin. You said the first time was when you went to inspect the 312th Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In fact, the first time I came cross the idea of the Mujahedin, the first time I heard that they had done something, was when I was a member of the joint commission in Vitez. This was after the events in Miletici. That's the first time I heard the term "Mujahedin." Up until then, it was a term that really wasn't familiar to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me start then by going back perhaps a step earlier. Did there come a time, sir, when you were aware of the presence of -- or when was the first time you became aware of the presence of these Mujahedin? Was it, as you just told us, when you were with the joint commission in Vitez?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Prior to that time, had you seen any of these individuals anywhere in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I hadn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So I take it then, as you told us yesterday, the first time you actually saw any Mujahedin was in July 1993?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, towards the end of July 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, exactly where it was, in what village or settlement or area, you first saw these individuals.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, if you were following, after having visited the 312th, I heard about these 30 Arabs. Up until then, I wasn't able to link this to the fact that it was the same group. After having visited the 312th, we visited the 306th Brigade; that was on the following day. I heard them calling them Muslim forces. Some people used the term "El Jihad." No one used the term "El Mujahedin," but this was a term that could also be heard. The first time I saw the Mujahedin was then. After having visited the 306th when we went down to Mehurici and when I asked to see these foreigners. They took me there, I saw a guard by a fence or a gate; he was armed. And I saw that he wasn't a local fighter. He didn't Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond have any insignia and he didn't look like a member of our forces either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you some questions in terms of clarifying or expanding upon what you've just told us. The first occasion when you saw these individuals, at the time you were conducting an inspection of the 312th, you told us that was in Bijelo Bucje. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I don't think this is what the witness said. He said he heard about 30 Arabs in the command. He didn't say that he had seen the people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, on the occasion when you were conducting an inspection of the 312th Brigade in July 1993, did you see any of these Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't. I didn't even go to the place where I was told that they were present. I was only informed of the fact that that group was there, but I never went to the area nor did I see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What did the commander or the person who told you about these 30 Mujahedin tell you about them?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll have to repeat this. He said that there was a group of 30 Arabs in an area, somewhere in that area, that they couldn't establish contact, that that was a problem, that they were requesting that they be resubordinated to the 312th or that they be taken from that area. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What if anything did you tell -- first of all, do you remember the name of the person who conveyed this information to you? Who told you this?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the commander of the battalion, Kobilic -- Kobilica, I'm not sure what his name was because I didn't know his name was before, but his name was Kobilic or Kobilica or something like that. He was the battalion commander in any event.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Once the battalion commander, the 312th battalion commander -- this was a battalion then of the 312th Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Once this battalion commander conveyed this information to you, what, if anything, did you say in response to him?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He provided me with this information while we were working. We'd spent the entire day working at the defence line. We had time to discuss the problem throughout the day, if there was any such problem; however, that was not the case. We were involved in issues of defending -- mounting a defence by his battalion in the forest. He only provided me with this information towards the end of the day after we had completed our visit. It was something he said by the way, so I didn't say anything. All I said was I would relay the information to my superior command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall if when he told you about these Mujahedin or foreign fighters that you were surprised by this?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He called them "Arabs;" he didn't use the term "Mujahedin." He said "Arabs," and that's what I wrote down. You know, I can't draft a report in the field; I draft reports in the corps command and I take care to make a precise recording of what people say. So I'm quite certain that he said "Arabs." That's what I wrote down. He did not use the term "the Mujahedin."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did it surprise you, sir, when this battalion commander informed you that there were approximately 30 Arabs in the vicinity?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Naturally, I was surprised.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: What questions, if any, did you ask him about these Arabs?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only question was whether he was in contact of any kind with them. He said he couldn't establish contact of any kind with them, and that's the extent of our discussion about them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you give him any advice or orders or communicate any information to him about what steps he might take with respect to these Arabs?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if you've been following this, but I was an officer in the operations and training organ of the 3rd Corps. I was one of the last links in that chain of command. I couldn't issue any orders in this respect. All I said was that I would inform the corps commander about the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But you don't recall suggesting that perhaps the battalion commander should attempt to obtain more information about these people or keep them under surveillance or try to gather any intelligence about these people for the benefit of the corps commander?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't provide such a suggestion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's turn now, sir, to --

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just clarify something. You know, the defence line was very near. If anyone meddled in the area of the defence line, this was very dangerous. I was afraid of making any changes. All I said was that I would inform the corps command and said that we would deal with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you this then, sir, in light of what you've just said: Did the battalion commander of the 312th inform you or say anything to you about whether or not those Arabs were manning part of that line, that defence line?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he said nothing about that. I understood that he had come across them there. According to what he said, it didn't appear that they were manning the defence line, at least that's not how I understood what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's turn now, sir, to I believe what you said was the following day when you were inspecting the 306th Mountain Brigade. It was on that occasion that you first personally observed Mujahedin or armed Arabs. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And that was in the vicinity of the village of Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. In the vicinity of Mehurici and a little further on from a mosque, which is in the centre of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, approximately how far from the centre of the village was the location where you saw these Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, perhaps I make a mistake now. I was there on that occasion and that was the only time. You can see the mosque on a slight slope. There's a dirt road. But it was at a distance of about 500 metres up to a kilometre, something like that. But I don't know the exact distance. It was a forested area, and that's where they were located. They were sheltered there; you couldn't see them from the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, to the best of your recollection which direction from the centre of the village of Mehurici these Mujahedin were located.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how to explain this. When you go to the village of Mehurici from the direction of Travnik, when you enter the village from the lower side there is a mosque to the left. The road continues by the mosque; it becomes a dirt road. And that was the area where they were located. I could draw you a sketch if you like.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In order to save time, sir, if you could perhaps tell us, was it to the north, south, east, west, north-west, south-east, which geographic direction from the centre of the village?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say, I really couldn't. But I was there. I see you're trying to convince me I wasn't there, but I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, sir, I'm not trying to convince you of anything. I'm simply asking you if you can tell us where this location that you saw these Mujahedin was located in reference to Mehurici. But I'll move on to another question. Can you describe for us what this location looked like where you saw these Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Passing by the mosque, right by the mosque, uphill along the dirt road there are two paths, one leading left and one right. When you take the right-hand one, you arrive at a wooded part of the terrain and there was a little house there like a holiday home. And I saw an -- a fence there, a wire-netting fence which may have been there before. I saw a ramp and a gate and some soldiers there. We tried to enter and somebody called out to that soldier that an officer from the corps command wanted to go in. And he made a gesture, indicated that we were not to come near. Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond And then we left, we turned away. That was all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, you just said that you saw a ramp and a gate and some soldiers there. Can you tell us approximately how many Mujahedin you saw?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see the soldiers inside; I just saw a guard standing in front, and I focused my attention on him because I wanted to go in. Inside I saw just a small building which reminded me of a holiday cottage. I didn't see anybody else, just this guard standing outside, but he didn't look like one of our fighters. You know what our people look like. You could see that he was darker skinned; I could see that he was a foreigner. It was easy to observe that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So that we're very clear then, sir, you saw one armed foreigner at the entrance to this summer cottage, and that was the only foreigner that you saw?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, do you recall who it was that escorted you from the 306th Brigade? Was it -- how many people were with you from the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that very clearly because I was a bit upset about that. There was Remzija Siljak, the chief of staff of the brigade; there was the commander of the 1st Battalion, Mirza Lubenovic; and myself. These were the people who were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, you told us just a moment ago on page 20, line 24, 25: "We tried to enter and somebody called out to that soldier that an officer from the corps command wanted to go in." Do you recall who called out to this armed guard?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly who it was. It might have been Remzija or Lubenovic, one of the two of them; I really don't remember exactly who said that. But they clearly gave him to understand that they had an officer of the corps with him and that he wanted to come in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what language did they address this soldier in, or this armed guard?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bosnian of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you tell us on any other occasion after this day whether you saw any armed Mujahedin up to the end of 1993 in Bosnia, Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was there as a commander, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So then, sir, so that we're absolutely clear, the only occasion in 1993 that you saw any Mujahedin, any armed foreign fighters, was on one day in July 1993 near Mehurici when you saw a single armed guard in front of a summer cottage? That's the only time?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, when you became the commander of the 306th Brigade, where was your headquarters?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The brigade command was in the village of Krpeljici in a private house.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And during the period I believe you said from August to November 1993, you were the brigade commander. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: During that time period when you were the 306th Mountain Brigade commander, was there a battalion of your brigade stationed or headquartered in the Mehurici primary school?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Where were the battalions of the 306th Brigade headquartered during the time you were the brigade commander?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Each battalion was in its area of defence, and that's where it had its command post. One of the battalions had its command post in the area of Paric Greda, which is behind Ljuta Greda, in the direction of the Serbian Montenegrin aggressor, where they were defending themselves and that's where they had their command. The 2nd Battalion had its command post in the village of Kljaci. This is the battalion holding positions in the direction of the extreme HVO. The 3rd Battalion had its command post of the village of -- what was its name now -- but it was in its -- Mosor, yes, that's the name of the village. Mosor. That was where the command of the 3rd Battalion was, and that's where they carried out their tasks against the HVO forces. Where the line of defence of that battalion was, that's where its command post was also.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I take it, sir, from your answer that the -- it certainly didn't appear in the English transcript that the command post that was in the area of Paric Greda was the 1st Battalion of the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Were you aware that earlier in 1993 there was a battalion of the 306th that was located or had a command post in Mehurici?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that. I was in the corps at that time. We didn't know what the command posts of the battalions was; we knew where the command posts of the brigades were. And it was difficult to get that information as well. And as for the lower-level units, the battalion command was supposed to know that.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The brigade command, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you, sir, about the El Mujahed unit and orders documents ordering that unit to be resubordinated to the 306th. You were asked some questions about this earlier today. Were you aware of any written documents from the 3rd Corps ordering that unit to be resubordinated to the 306th?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But it's your testimony here today that in fact that never happened?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so, it didn't happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Once it became clear to you that that was not happening, what steps did you take to inform your chain of command about this apparent failure of that unit to follow orders?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember whether I drew up any written document saying that the unit had not resubordinated itself to me, but as we said yesterday or today offensive combat activities were being planned. And when you're preparing a unit for something like that, you don't have time for correspondence; you have to implement your written orders. After the combat activities had been carried out, it was clear to my immediate superior that the unit had not been there with me. He could see that from the reports. I don't remember whether I told him right away that the unit had not come under my command because I had my hands full preparing my unit for combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us a little bit about these combat activities that you were planning or preparing your unit for at that time.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my, let's say, surprise because you have to know that I'd been there for only about a week and I still hadn't found my bearings, I felt as if I had been parachuted on to Mars. It was very difficult for me to find my bearings in this new situation. And I was pre-occupied with these combat activities; they took up all of my attention and energy. Now, looking at it with hindsight, I didn't really find my way in the best possible manner. There was an area where my brigade and the 305th Mountain Brigade were to join up, and this was a very small area and this -- all this was very frustrated -- frustrating for me. I don't know what details you'd like to know about these combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you a slightly different question, sir, and that is: At that point in time, in August 1993, as you were planning these combat activities, did you have sufficient manpower in the 306th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the operations group, General Alagic thought I had; I of course thought I didn't. But I had to carry out the order of my superior commander. So I set apart a unit the strength of a company and trained it for the forthcoming combat activities; that's the way I prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you became aware of the order resubordinating the El Mujahed unit to your brigade, did you know anything about the El Mujahed unit such as its size or its capabilities or any combat experience that that unit might have?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have partly answered the question. I was supposed to know all Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond that or to find out all that when the unit joined me, what its numbers were, what equipment it had, what its combat experience was, what its logistical support was in order to use it properly. I didn't know any of this. One thing was clear to me, that this unit -- that somebody was trying to bring this unit into line, to turn them into proper soldiers and bring them into line when carrying out combat activity. And I understood that this unit had finally been established because they were sending it to me, but I didn't know any of these other elements that I needed to know as a commander, which I've just listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, you've told us that when you were planning this operation or these combat-related activities you didn't think you had enough manpower. Here was an order ordering this El Mujahed unit to be resubordinated to your brigade, which would seem to be a solution in part to the manpower problems you had. And I'm wondering what steps you took to contact your immediate superior, General Alagic, or failing that the corps commander who issued this order to the El Mujahed unit to say, hey, where are these guys? I need these guys. You've ordered them to be resubordinated to me and I don't know where they are, and I need them. Did you take any steps like that, sir?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, I'll tell you again. In all that chaos in which I found myself, I assessed that it would be easier and less painful for me to set apart from all three battalions of the brigade and even from the staff units to set apart men for active combat activity rather than to wait for someone who may or may not arrive. Because Commander Alagic told us more than once, When you get an order don't come to me with complaints, requests, or problems. You must tell me those much earlier. It was easier for me to set apart a company, and it wasn't easy but I did it, and I thought I could carry out the task with that company, whether this unit arrived or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, I take it, sir, from that answer that you did not contact either General Alagic or the 3rd Corps commander, General Hadzihasanovic, in order to determine what had happened to the El Mujahed unit that had been ordered to be resubordinated to your brigade by the 3rd Corps commander?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for my immediate superior, I cannot assert with any certainty, but he knew about the situation -- or rather I can't say whether he knew or not. He may have been told briefly, orally. There were only two or three days before the start of combat activities. As for the commander of the 3rd Corps, I had the operations group and I didn't need to go over their heads and inform the commander about my problems. Commander Alagic knew about this because after all this was over I heard that this unit was to have been resubordinated to the operations group and that this had not happened. Yet again, it hadn't happened. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me turn to a slightly different subject, sir. If you still have the binder in front of you I'd ask you to turn to the second document under IV. This is a document which the Defence has shown you earlier under --

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what section is this?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: -- section IV, the Mujahedins, the final section. The tabs at the top indicate the sections, and then if you go to document 2. It's a --

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I've just found it. Mujahedin, document 2, 1360. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, sir, that's document 1. It would be the one after the next tab. It has in handwriting: DH270.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's a mistake in the interpretation, it's 270.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] DH270?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, DH270. We briefly looked at this document earlier today. Can you confirm for us, sir, that you are the author of this document which is dated 2 August, 1993?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes I am the author.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to draw your attention to the final line of the second paragraph on the first page. If you look at the first page, the second paragraph.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which page?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Page one.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The second paragraph, the final line of that paragraph. There is a reference there --

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: There is a reference there to Muslimanske Snage?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, as the author of this document, can you tell us what you were talking about when you wrote Muslimanske Snage in your document?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was referring to these foreigners because if you look at the last paragraph on the next page it says: "Resolve the issue of the El Jihad formation. This was what I meant when I referred to the Muslim forces. One officer said these are Muslim forces, another would refer to them in this other way, and then you didn't know what their name was really. That's the reason for these differences. These were the foreigners who were there, whom the common people sometimes refer to as the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So in this document that you wrote, DH270, reference to the Muslim forces on the first page and reference to the El Jihad on the second page are both references to foreign fighters, Mujahedin?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yes. Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, can you elaborate or give us any additional information about what the reference on the first page to: "Communication sent to all villages from the Muslim forces summoning soldiers for a 40-day training." Can you tell us anything about that?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All I can tell you is what I heard then from the battalion commander, and this was the following: In the context of people or men leaving his unit to join various other units he said that these Muslim forces - and he himself may have used this expression, I'm not sure - that they were recruiting, buying, coaxing, or trying to attract these fighters to come to them for training and nobody knew whether they would come back to our units or not. And he said if this went on, the defence line would be in danger. Allegedly they were offering them money, uniforms, good weapons, so that men, especially the younger men, left without asking anyone if they could leave. But some of them came back.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we turn now to the second page of this document under the heading "Proposed Measures," number 4, point number 4. Now, sir, you've addressed this document to the -- both to the commander of the operations group and to the 3rd Corps. And I'm wondering if you can tell us, sir, a little bit of information about proposed measure number 4?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I sent this to the command of the 306th, and I acted as a soldier in the simplest way. All the armed forces in an area should be put under the command of the brigade commander. And I asked that this formation - and here I use the name "El Jihad," I didn't know actually what their name really was - that in terms of their place in the establishments something should be done, either that they should be declared a paramilitary unit if they didn't want to take orders, or that they should be put under somebody's command. They couldn't act on their own initiative. I realised that there was no -- no one commanding them when I saw that camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you perhaps explain to us or elaborate upon the notion of to proclaim or declare them a paramilitary unit. What exactly does that mean?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would mean that they were not a regular unit, not part of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, not a unit such as the units of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And who would make such a declaration or proclamation indicating that these people were not a unit of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only guess, probably the top of the army, somebody from the very top. It couldn't be done by a local commander I assume, as far as I Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, when you made this proposal you told us that this was addressed -- or you sent this to the command of the 306th. It seems to be addressed to the commander of the 306th, the commander of the OG Bosanska Krajina, and the 3rd Corps. And you're proposing that one of those three formations, the 306th or the OG Bosanska Krajina or the 3rd Corps, could resolve this problem. Isn't that what paragraph 4 under Proposed Measures says?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You couldn't really say that because the lower command couldn't solve those problems without a superior command. The lower-level commands received this for their information. I didn't state that, but that's what actually happened. The only command that could solve this problem was the corps command, but evidently it wasn't fully familiar with the situation. And I from the corps command learned about something like this for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, when you say "proclaimed them paramilitaries," immediately thereafter it makes reference to the corps command organ for mobilisation. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These personnel matters would be dealt with within that organ, but that organ couldn't deal with the entire issue. They couldn't do all the work necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you make any proposed recommendations to the 3rd Corps commander that he should seek some kind of higher authority to deal with this problem?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as this matter is concerned, no. A lot of similar reports would arrive in the corps command, and usually a regular procedure would be followed. A report would be sent to the operations centre, the operations centre would process it, and then the usual procedure would be followed. I didn't forward this report to the commander myself; it was forwarded by the regular mail service.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, you told us earlier that you only saw this one Mujahedin during 1993, and I'm wondering how you came to a conclusion that no one was commanding them when you saw that camp based on this observation that you had and which you had explained to us?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When visiting the unit -- when you visit a unit, you never visit a lower-level unit if the commander isn't present. So I visited that with the commander of the 1st Battalion, Lubenovic. I've already mentioned this. He mentioned a significant problem, namely the fact that those soldiers would go to other units, and he said that he had no control over the fact that they would join other units. All those that left were no longer in the 1st Battalion, but they would also go to the 314th, to the 17th. He didn't have command over the 17th either. So as far as he was concerned that soldier had disappeared. And he also mentioned that the Muslim forces - I think that's what he called them at the time - he said that the Muslim forces were going after these people, that they wouldn't return that he said that he had no contact with them. He had nothing to with this. And he said that he wouldn't be able to organise any shifts. If they had been under his command, there wouldn't have been any problems as far as rotating the men at that location was concerned. He said that if things condition in this way, it will not be possible to replenish units. Then I came to the conclusion that he had no command over the units that his soldiers were joining, and that was especially noticeable when we went up to that location where we were seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, because of the fact that this was a problem that occurred in a number of different brigades, that's why this problem needed to be resolved at the corps level. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was resolved, to the extent that this was possible. New units were formed and in that area you heard about the fact that the 27th Motorised Brigade was formed, so action was taken. Because look, as far as these troops are concerned, the ones we're talking about, if that's what we can call them, they didn't have any tasks. They were quite simply there. They didn't go anywhere; whereas, other units had combat tasks. The 27th and the 306th were constantly manning the defence lines. So the corps command did take this situation into account. They tried to replenish certain units, deploy units in the area concerned, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I note the time. This might be an appropriate point to take our first technical break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll have our technical break now. It's almost half past 4.00, and we will resume at about 5 to 5.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will now resume. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I'd ask now that we turn our attention to a slightly different matter but one which you are also asked about earlier this afternoon, and that is the steps taken by the assistant commander for security of the 306th Brigade with respect to the events in Maline Bikosi in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could, if he doesn't have it in front of him, again have before him DK17.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you -- let me ask you, sir, while that document is being returned to you, do you recall or can you perhaps tell us about how you first became aware of the need to conduct an investigation or an inquiry into the events of June 1993 in Maline, in Bikosi?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before these events, before I arrived in the brigade I was aware of combat activities that had been ongoing in the field. I didn't know all the details, but I know there was fighting. I know that the 306th Brigade and its command had been broken up, split up. The fighting was very heavy; that was the initial information I had before I became the commander of the 306th Brigade. Having assumed that post I found out that I was being asked to provide a report on these events. The first time I found out about this was when I received a written order requesting that I provide them with information about what had happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you if you recall approximately when you received that order or became aware of the need to conduct such an inquiry?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, it was after these combat operations had been conducted, sometime in October, I can't remember the exact date. But that order arrived in my command in the month of October 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, during the time period that you were still with the 3rd Corps in early to mid-June 1993 whether you'd heard from any source about any potential criminal activity in the area of Maline Bikosi or any massacre? Had you heard anything about that at all during the time period you were still with the 3rd Corps command?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was in the corps command, combat reports would arrive from the field sent by those units engaged in combat there. None of those reports mentioned these events, so I had no information about this. We received reports on combat, on the problems encountered while carrying out combat operations. I remember that the 300 -- the command of the 306th Brigade had been split up, they were located in two or three places. I remember those alarming reports about the events there, but it wasn't possible to draw a conclusion from these reports that anything like the events described had actually happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether you heard or received any reports about the presence of Mujahedin in the area around Maline Bikosi on the 8th or 9th of June, 1993, from any units?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have said, I never came across such information in the reports I had access to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, whether you heard any discussions at any -- had perhaps any meetings of the 3rd Corps command any -- or received from any source any information about complaints by the HVO or any Bosnian-Croat entity about alleged massacres in Maline Bikosi on or about the 8th or 9th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember anything of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So the first time then, sir, that you had any information that Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond there was potentially something wrong or something wrong had happened in Maline Bikosi was in October 1993 when you received an order to conduct some type of inquiry. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but when I arrived in the unit, naturally I tried to learn as many details as possible about the unit over which I was to have command. I spoke to the men about various issues, and in particular we spoke about the combat operations very frequently. I found out about the fact that part of the command was in Lager and another part in Mehurici, and another part by Rudnik. They spoke about the combat situation in that area. So I drew certain conclusions as to how all of these events had unfolded. But they never mentioned anything of that kind. I really never had such information. The first time I found out something about this subject was when I received the order to answer some questions about the events in question. There were certain doubts at the time, certain things were suspected.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you perhaps inform us about what these doubts or certain things that were suspected, can you tell us what was in doubt or what was suspected.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't suspect anything, but the fact that someone asked me for a report about those events showed that they were requiring reliable information. Again, since these events had happened earlier on, I was wondering why I was being asked to do something then. I wasn't there; I only had superficial information about these events. So that would be the extent of what I suspected.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, can you tell us please what steps you took once you received the order to conduct this inquiry into events in Maline Bikosi on or about the 8th of June, 1993.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to correct you. I wasn't provided with a request to launch an investigation. I was ordered to draft a report on everything I knew about the matter; this was an order from the corps command. And on the basis of this order, I didn't believe it was necessary to carry out some kind of an investigation. I spoke to my closest associates, the chief of staff, the deputy commander. I spoke to the men who worked with me, and I forwarded the document I received to the security organ so that they could take all the necessary measures and report back to me on what they had done. In the meantime there was fighting, various other things were going on, so that's not the only subject I was occupied with during that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you please -- you've told us the positions of the persons that you spoke to concerning this order. Can you perhaps inform us of the names of these individuals that you spoke with concerning this order that you received.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chief of staff Remzija Siljak, I would speak to him about everything else as well. I think the deputy commander was Munib Kadric [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And you told us you forwarded the document to the security organ. Can you tell us what assets or resources you had in the 306th Brigade in the security organ.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question. What sort of resources are you referring to, personnel?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let's talk about personnel, sir. How many people were in the security organ, what were their names, what training did they have, what experience in security matters, these types -- these types of issues.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My assistant for security, I know his surname, Delalic, but I have forgotten his first name. And there was an officer who was present there, too; they formed the security organ. There was a subordinate unit that they were in charge of, it was a military police platoon. And those were the resources. As far as training is concerned, as far as their knowledge is concerned, I found them in the state they were in when I arrived there. I didn't have conditions to train anyone, let alone these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall when you first spoke to the security organ or the personnel in the security organ if you spoke to one person or did you speak to more than one person about this order that you received, and if so can you recall who you spoke to?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already said, things take place very rapidly in war. It's as if you are on an assembly line. As the commander of the unit -- well, I've told you how I arrived at that post and I've told you how I felt at that time. I think I sent the document to where it was supposed to go, to the security organ, and they were to report back to me as soon as possible, in particular because they were participants. But I didn't speak to anyone else from the security organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, could we very briefly go into private session for a couple of questions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are back in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you -- would it refresh your memory if I told you that the assistant commander for security within the 306th Brigade was Asim Delalic?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you at that point in time or any time subsequent to that have any opportunity to get to know Mr. Delalic in terms of his professional experience or training in order to be an assistant commander for security?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I arrived in the 306th Brigade, I didn't know Mr. Delalic. I only knew the chief of staff, Remzija Siljak. I didn't know which schools he had completed, I knew nothing about his training. So I knew nothing about anyone else, apart from Remzija Siljak. We knew each other from before. I really didn't know the other men who were present there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you at any point in time when you were the commander of that brigade or perhaps at some later time come to learn anything about Mr. Delalic's background or experience as it related to military security matters?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. In the brigade we didn't even have files on those officers, so I didn't even know the schools that certain officers had completed, let alone other forms of training that they had had.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what steps you took once you received information back from the assistant commander Asim Delalic with respect to events in Maline Bikosi on 8th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I received that document, a report was written for the corps command, which was based on the document. Various people had been killed at the time, but this was the result of combat operations. I think that that is what he wrote.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, who was involved in the combat? When you say these persons were killed as a result of combat operations, do you know who was involved in the combat?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I think the witness Blank page inserted to ensure the pagination between the English and French transcripts correspond has already answered this question. He has already said what he knew about the combat in the month of June, and it's obvious that there is nothing that the witness can add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In order to assist the Judges and inform the Judges, who participated in the combat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have already said that I know that HVO forces and army forces were involved in the fighting; I knew nothing else and that was the case while I was still in the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, at any point in time did anyone from the 306th Mountain Brigade or any other unit of the 3rd Corps of the ABiH inform you or otherwise tell you anything about the involvement of any Mujahedin in the area of Maline Bikosi on 8th June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, although I spoke to various people about all sorts of subjects, in fact I spoke to my associates, this is something that they never mentioned. We spoke about very subjects, but they never mentioned this. We spoke about an HVO attack against certain villages, they mentioned their lack of organisation when conducting combat operations. As far as I could understand the situation, they barely managed to organise themselves again after that combat. Those are the only things that we discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, did you discuss with Mr. Asim Delalic what steps he took in order to provide you with the information about what happened in Maline Bikosi on the 8th of June, 1993?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that. I can't remember all the conversations I had. Perhaps I did speak to him about this, perhaps not. You know, when the document was drafted in such clear terms -- well, the situation was quite clear to me as someone who has -- as someone who had just arrived. Sir, I, quite simply, did not suspect that anything else had happened. I trusted and believed my officers. There was no reason for me to suspect anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I guess, sir, my question goes more towards whether you made any inquiries to Mr. Delalic about the methodology he used in coming to the conclusion he did. Did you say -- did you ask him, did you interview witnesses or did you speak to soldiers who were present or did you review documents? I'm just curious if you made any inquiries to him how he came to this conclusion or whether he volunteered that information orally to you and told you, this is what I did, here's the steps I took, here's how I reached the conclusions I reached.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My information about these events were equal to zero. I had only information about combat activities. When a document arrived asking for something, again I didn't even consider it all that important. I just indicated where necessary that a report be made. As for the methods he used, I didn't discuss them with him because I had no suspicions. For me, what was written down there was sufficient. I didn't know. I really didn't know anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll give the floor to the Defence now if they have any re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The Defence has a few additional questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My learned friend asked you about the number of battalions. Tell me please, as in early August you were touring the 306th Brigade and you said that on that occasion you talked to the commander of the 1st Battalion, Commander Lubenovic. This was a battalion of the 306th Brigade, the 1st Battalion, and its commander was Lubenovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you became the commander of the 306th Mountain Brigade, was commander Lubenovic still in this brigade with his then-1st Battalion?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Where was this battalion at that time?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was being, rather the 27th was being made up of that battalion and refugees from various places, and it was Mehuric. It was a brigade that was in the process of being formed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: And were all the men from that previous battalion, the fighters, the command, the police department attached to that battalion, were they all transferred to the 27th Brigade or did they remain under your command?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were all transferred to the 27th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: When you received a request that you answer questions put by the command of the 3rd Corps, you as a commander had no authority over the people who were previously in the 1st Battalion of the 306th which had been in Mehurici. Did you have any authority over that battalion at that time?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course not. I even told Commander Imamovic, who came to take over the 27th Brigade, about this. The only thing I did was that with Commander Alagic of the 1st Operations Group we visited the command of this new 27th Brigade, where Lubenovic and that battalion were. We visited this command which was in a house on the outskirts of Mehurici and I had no contact with that unit. A new commander had been appointed.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: In October 1993 this brigade was already fully functional. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please now look again at the document under number 2, your report from your visit to the 306th Mountain Brigade. Do you have this document, DH270? Not that one. In section IV, Mujahedin, the second document is DH270 and it's report on the inspection of the 306th Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: VEZIR JUSUFSPAHIC [Resumed]
